title: Using AI to unpack the bi-directional association between adolescent social media exposure and mental health and well being
text:
With notable increases in rates of adolescent depression over the last decade, many researchers are looking
to understand the causes, with social media being a main focus. The current study will help address this
research question by following adolescents over 2.5 years. This time period will allow us to see how
adolescents’ mental health and social media change over time, including how mental health and social media
may impact each other; and what might help explain why and when they do.

title: The mitochondrial aspects of health disparity of hepatocellular carcinoma in Hispanic population
text:
In the United States, HCC is one of the fastest growing causes of cancer related death with a 5-
year survival of less than 12%. Notably, this disease burden is disproportionately expressed
among different demographic ethnic groups as the incidence and mortality rates in the US are
about three times as high in Hispanics as in non-Hispanic whites in both genders. Our research
is expected to generate a mechanistic linkage among the mitochondrial genotype, HCV infection,
mitochondrial function and tumorigenesis in HCC, a disease that is over-represented in the
Hispanic population.

title: Liquid-Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) System
text: The LCMS system will enable critical biomedical investigations addressing significant public health challenges in the Appalachian region, including substance use disorders, medication safety, and other health conditions commonly seen in rural communities. Faculty researchers currently face substantial financial and logistical barriers to progress as they must outsource sample analysis to distant facilities, with no comparable instrumentation available within our region. Beyond advancing research, this technology will provide students across multiple health science disciplines with hands-on experience using sophisticated analytical methods increasingly essential in modern healthcare and pharmaceutical settings.

title: Delineation of unique flagellar proteins in spirochetes
text:
Spirochetes cause several serious diseases in humans and periplasmic flagellar motility is crucial for virulence by all
pathogenic spirochetes. The novel studies outlined in this proposal are to delineate periplasmic flagellar assembly,
orientation, bacterial morphology, and motility that are distinctive in the spirochetes. The virulence-associated flagellar
structural proteins can lead to the development of a structure-based pharmacological agent to treat or prevent diseases
caused by the spirochetes.

title: Development of platform technology to measure kinetics and equilibrium concentration of sickle hemoglobin polymerization in single RBCs for drug potency assessment and patient risk stratification
text:
There are no effective treatments for sickle cell anemia, a disease affecting millions
worldwide that is caused by the pathologic polymerization of sickle hemoglobin inside red
blood cells when they become deoxygenated, but there are several very exciting new
approaches in development including gene therapy, gene editing with CRISPR, hemoglobin
gene regulation, and hemoglobin oxygen afϐinity modulation. All of these treatments work
by reducing the amount of hemoglobin polymer that will form at a given oxygen tension,
but we currently have no way to measure the amount of polymer in individual RBCs, and
we therefore do not know how intense each treatment needs to be for each patient, or
which treatment or combination of treatments will be most effective for each patient. This
project will validate a platform enabling deϐinition of therapeutic windows for current and
experimental treatments as well as their combinations, providing a tool to speed drug
development and enable personalization of current and future treatment for sickle cell
patients.

title: The neuropathology of mild traumatic brain injury in Alzheimer's disease
text:
This proposal addresses a critical need for both our older and younger populations of veterans. Head
trauma is a risk factor for both Alzheimer disease and Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy, a
neurodegenerative disease caused by repetitive mild traumatic brain injury. Soldiers have always been
at risk for head injury and this is particularly the case for OEF/OIF veterans, many of who have
experienced explosive blast injury and participated in contact sports. There is a critical need to
understand the mechanisms and risk factors underlying this injury to facilitate prevention, diagnosis,
and treatment. The aging veteran population and high rate of head injury will lead to daunting costs and
responsibilities for the VA if research aimed at translating mechanisms into biomarkers and treatments
is not developed. Improved understanding of the role of cerebrovascular remodeling in the development
of neurodegenerative disease may lead to new treatment options and directions for interventions.

title: Modeling Ataxia Telangiectasia (A-T) in a Novel Laminar System for Human Stem Cell-Derived Purkinje Cells
text:
Ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T) is a genetic disorder characterized by cerebellar degeneration, telangiectasia,
increased susceptibility to cancer, and immunodeficiency for which there is no cure. It affects ~1:40,000-
1:100,000 live births worldwide. In the proposed research, we will create the first model system using induced
pluripotent stem cells from A-T patients to study human cerebellar Purkinje cells affected by A-T, and will use a
novel laminar system to explore how the disease progresses in A-T iPSC-PCs, including changes in neuronal
development, physiological properties and the underlying ionic currents, gene expression and protein
expression.

title: Genomic Workforce Development Core
text:
There is an urgent national need to grow a strong genomic workforce which includes populations
underrepresented in biomedical research. We propose a streamlined educational feeder pipeline called
PoWER-G (Promotion of Workforce Employment and Readiness in Genomics) providing an innovative “on-the-
degree” training and professional development platform which draws upon the substantial student diversity
within the University of Hawaii system. Knowledge generated by this pilot project will lead to development of a
formal 1-year Graduate Certificate Program to promote diversity in the genomic workforce and to continue to
meet the exponential growth in genomics.

title: Discovering protein networks underlying regulated exocytosis
text:
Regulated exocytosis is central to a wide range of fundamental physiological processes. Mechanistic insights
gleaned from this study will substantially broaden our knowledge of regulated exocytosis and will shed light upon
the pathogenesis of diseases linked to regulated exocytosis.

title: Elucidating the biophysical basis of repeatability in the evolution of drug resistance
text:
Pathogens often evolve different resistance mutations across species, even when drugs target a conserved
protein site, hindering the development of broad-spectrum therapies. This project will quantify the repeatability
of resistance pathways across species of a model pathogen and determine the mechanism of divergence by
elucidating how mutational effects on protein activity and folding stability, biophysical factors known to shape
resistance pathways, differ across homologs. These findings will inform the design of more durable and broadly
effective antimicrobial treatments.

title: Defining Optimal Radiotherapy Dose and Fractionation in Combination with Preoperative Immuno-Chemotherapy in Early-Stage Triple Negative Breast Cancer
text:
Defining a forward path for successful implementation of preoperative radiotherapy boost to enhance the efficacy
of standard neoadjuvant immunotherapy-chemotherapy in early-stage triple negative breast cancer represents
a novel and potentially groundbreaking treatment paradigm. This randomized phase II study, P-RAD: A
Randomized Trial of Preoperative Pembrolizumab with No, Low or High Dose RADiation Therapy in HER2-
Negative Breast Cancer, will define the optimal RT dose (0Gy, 9Gy or 24Gy) for the radiotherapy boost to
combine with immune checkpoint inhibitor and chemotherapy. In addition to the co-primary endpoints of
pathologic complete response rate and change in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, the study will provide unique
insights through a comprehensive assessment of serial tumor tissue and blood samples in correlative studies.

title: Addressing Protein Synthesis Regulation within Small Numbers of Discrete Neurons
text:
RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) and ribosomes are key molecules that drive and regulate post-
transcriptional gene expression. RBPs are implicated in many different diseases including cancer and
brain and neurodegenerative diseases (Fragile X syndrome, ALS). Ribosome-based genetic tools such
as Ribo-TRIBE, Ribo-STAMP and Nanobody-editing will enable different areas of biology and medicine
to address gene expression regulation within very small numbers of specific cells or neurons.

title: Trait-Based Metagenomics for Predicting Microbiome Dynamics
text:
The proposed research will develop new AI/ML-based methods to infer the traits of
microorganisms directly from their genomes and from microbiome sequencing data. We
will leverage these trait inference methods to subsequently build improved models of
microbiome dynamics to predict how the composition of individual microbiomes will
change over time.

title: Subcortico-Cortical Mechanisms of Sensorimotor Coordination, Integration, and Learning
text:
Dysfunctions of sensorimotor behaviors are among the most common and devastating aspects of neurological
disorders. Converging evidence from humans and animal models indicate that the cerebello-thalamocortical
and basal ganglia-thalamocortico pathways play critical and complementary roles in sensorimotor behaviors.
However, we do not have a coherent understanding of how these pathways support the basic building blocks
of sensorimotor behavior including coordination, integration, and learning. In this proposal, we will combine
large-scale multi-region electrophysiology and multi-region neural network modeling to tease apart the
complementary roles of these pathways in sensorimotor behavior. This work will elucidate the computational
principles, anatomical substrates, and physiological mechanisms of sensorimotor function, and promises to
facilitate the development of diagnostics and treatments for victims of neurological disorders.

title: Natural-based therapies for sensory disorders
text:
This proposal exploits the beneficial characteristics of a natural product, piperlongumine and piperlongumine
derivatives, for protection against hearing loss in patients receiving antibiotic treatment for severe infections.
Accomplishing these pre-clinical studies will allow us to gather the necessary scientific information to advance
piperlongumine or its derivatives into future clinical trials.

title: Enhancing Clinical Trial Analysis Leveraging Baseline Neuroimaging Data
text:
It is well-known in clinical trial methodology that accounting for measured baseline covariates can produce more
efficient estimators of both the treatment effect and the treatment effect heterogeneity by reducing the standard
error of the estimators. Moreover, unaddressed treatment effect heterogeneity can also mask treatment effects,
causing trials to fail despite real benefits to some patients. To address challenges with utilizing baseline
neuroimaging in clinical trials, we develop semiparametric statistical machine learning methods for efficient
treatment effect and treatment effect heterogeneity estimation in clinical trials of treatments for Alzheimer’s
disease and late-life depression.

title: Brain structure and function in infants
text:
Resting-state (RS) neural activity shows rapid changes across the first years of life (the background
against which brain function and behavior emerge), with RS activity in older children and adults
indexing the inhibition of task-irrelevant processes, associated with top-down cognitive control
processes, central to how local networks process information, and associated with our ability to
quickly process information. Our understanding of RS activity in infants and toddlers is limited by
challenges that have so far hindered research in this area, with this project making progress via (1)
the use of a RS task optimized for infants and toddlers, (2) using recently developed algorithms to
more accurately measure RS activity, (3) obtaining measures of RS activity in brain space to test
theories associating RS neural activity with brain structure, chemistry, and developmental
milestones, and (4) obtaining temporally dense brain measures as understanding brain
development requires assessing maturational processes. In this prospective cohort design, brain
development and behavior will be examined at baseline in infants 0 to 4 months (N=70) and then
longitudinally at 4-month intervals with the final visit at 12 to 16 months (4 visits in total), with finding
greatly extending our understanding of infant/toddler resting-state neural activity.

title: Advanced microscope technologies for single-molecule functional analyses of stereocilia components necessary for normal human hearing
text:
Sensorineural hearing loss is a common disease with a prevalence of 20% in the United States, which can
impede development of speech and language skills in children and cognitive functions in adults. Stereocilia of
inner ear hair cells are organelles that function as biological mechanical switches essential for normal hearing
and often degenerate in individuals with sensorineural hearing loss. Single-molecule functional analyses
proposed in this study are experimental frameworks to elucidate the molecular dynamics in wild type stereocilia
with the goal of identifying therapeutic targets for malfunctioning stereocilia.

title: Regulation of Overall Cell Numbers During Epithelial Tissue Homeostasis and Pathogenesis
text:
The rate of cellular turnover slows during aging, can be accelerated during injury and repair, and is precociously
stimulated during carcinogenesis; but the mechanisms guiding turnover in living tissues is not well understood.
The proposed studies will determine how the elimination of unfit cells by extrusion from epithelia stimulates the
nearby stem cells to generate new cells and maintain overall cell numbers in the tissue. Discoveries arising from
this work will provide new insights into mechanisms that can be harnessed to promote cellular replacement or
prevent the unwanted addition of new cells.
